Final project · Kush Dhall

Going Home

Hospital discharge papers → a plan a family can follow,
checked against the original, in their language.

It restates the hospital's plan. It never diagnoses, changes a dose or gives medical advice.

https://github.com/kush-kd/going-home

The problem: the hand-off home

  • ~1 in 5 patients has an adverse event after discharge, mostly from medicines
  • Only 56% know the doses of their new medicines
  • 81% of discharge instructions are above a 6th-grade reading level
  • 25M people in the US have limited English

Forster 2003; phone follow-up study; Am J Med 2025; MPI. Full citations in the report.

What's new

  • Portals and printouts: same hard text, usually English only
  • Reminder apps (Medisafe): every medicine typed in by hand
  • Chatbots: explain, but can invent doses, with no checks and no plan
  • Hospital AI summaries: built for clinicians; studies found omissions and invented medicines
  • Going Home: verified against the source, actionable (timetable, calendar, print chart), asks instead of guessing, 9 languages
  • A planning tool, not a medical one: it restates, never recommends

How the agents work

Reader: Opus · Checker (with MCP tools: list_medication_lines, search_document, check_quote, verify_item), Explainer, Transcriber: Sonnet · all via claude -p on a Claude subscription · one capped repair round · per-call dollar cap

Demo: Mr. Chen, 79, in Chinese

Timetable with tick boxes and the STOP box · every card shows the English source sentence, ✓ matched

Warning signs, visits, questions

911 vs call-the-clinic signs with tap-to-call numbers · vague orders become questions, never guesses

  • Opus only where accuracy matters; caching cut a repeat run 41%
  • Giving the Checker real tools cut cost $0.25 → $0.20 per plan and repairs to 0 of 5

Safety

  • Hidden and visible prompt injection removed by code before any agent reads
  • Restates, never recommends: code blocks added doses, purposes and tips
  • Every dose and number matched to the source, or it stays off the timetable
  • One capped repair round, 8 calls max, token and daily caps
  • 31 automated tests; a real false positive caught and fixed

What's next

  • Pilot with discharge nurses: bedside review before the family leaves
  • Read-back questions for the caregiver, flagged to the care team
  • SMS reminders, shared caregiver view, refill nudges
  • Larger evaluation on de-identified real papers, photos and scans

Going Home doesn't replace the care team. It makes sure the family leaves with the plan they were given.
